claims.statement: Orienting/reorienting and disengagement are distinguishable operations within attentional selection and control, while capture refers to involuntary priority rather than every orienting event.
Attentional lapses are transient failures within sustained/vigilant attention and are distinct from the longer time-on-task vigilance decrement.
Selection competition is a system-level description of interacting priority signals rather than a sufficiently independent latent construct for its own L2 node.
Awareness/appraisal of a knowledge gap can trigger epistemic curiosity but is one pathway among several and does not deterministically produce information seeking.

Competence-seeking is too overlapping with learning-progress/mastery processes at the current L2 resolution and is better represented inside the learning-progress module unless future evidence separates it.

Subjective costs, anticipated outcome value, experienced outcome value, and punishment/loss value are separable components of value-based judgment and learning, though reward and punishment evidence is asymmetrical.
Mixed emotions are a robust and measurable co-occurrence of differently valenced affective states and are not captured by a single bipolar valence score.
Confrontation/mobilization can be represented as an action tendency emerging from appraisal-emotion processes, but its mapping to any one discrete emotion is conditional.
Personal relevance valuation is better represented as a cross-core pathway from self-relevance into subjective value than as an independent L2 construct.
Generic action activation is too broad and overlaps arousal plus specific action tendencies; retain the differentiated tendency nodes instead.
Generic 'positive emotion' and 'negative emotion' buckets are not sufficiently specific L2 mechanisms; future emotion-specific constructs should be added at finer resolution when materially needed.
Personal self-concept is a legitimate representation of self-related attributes, roles and meanings and can be distinguished from momentary social self-categorization.
Intergroup boundary maintenance is better treated as a possible identity-protective response/pathway rather than an independent L2 construct at this resolution.
Prior source performance and track record contribute to reliability/credibility judgments and can be represented as a history-based reliability assessment distinct from a one-shot cue.
Motive authenticity is not yet sufficiently separable from perceived genuineness and benevolence to justify a standalone L2 node.
Observed behavioral consistency is source-history evidence feeding reliability judgment, not necessarily an independent latent trust state.
Relationship maintenance is a validated dimension of enduring parasocial relationship and is separable from intimacy and real-life relationship intention.

Current PSI evidence validates an episode-level interaction experience, but does not justify treating cognitive engagement and affective response as independent canonical L2 PSI constructs; keep them as possible lower-level features.
Exposure history is contextual/memory provenance that conditions familiarity and relationship development rather than a standalone connection state.
Perceived relational closeness substantially overlaps the validated PSR intimacy dimension and should be merged to avoid redundant L2 representation.
Parasocial attachment is currently under-studied relative to PSI/PSR; separation/loss sensitivity is even less established, so neither should remain an active canonical L2 node yet.
Affective expression is a defensible motive for interpersonal transmission distinct from incidental arousal and from the observed sharing act.
Audience inhibition is better represented as the downstream effect of audience composition plus privacy/reputational cost, rather than an independent transmission motive/state.
Reinforcement sensitivity is primarily an individual-difference/moderator construct at this architecture level rather than a core learning operation.
Habitual control strength is a derived summary over context-response control, automaticity, and outcome sensitivity, not a primitive L2 mechanism.
A discrete habit-goal arbitration mechanism is one viable model but not the only supported architecture; it belongs in competing model hypotheses rather than the canonical neuron set.
Habit override/suppression is better represented as an emergent outcome of goal-directed control, context change, and contingency/outcome revaluation than as an independent primitive node.
